native_observations: The exact shared constructor dereferences the supplied method value at +0x8, +0x4C, and +0x52 while deriving the delegate invoke fields.

managed_callback_boundary.boundary_conclusion: The exports can support an adapter only after code is already executing inside the game process. They do not expose external IPC and do not create an arbitrary native function as a managed System.Action.

candidate_comparison.limitations: Requires a supported in-process entry and valid managed Action; queued items have no removal API.

Builds a NextFrame async state machine, chains ContinueWith(callback), then Forget(exceptionHandler). ForceToLua is metadata, not an external IPC entry; it also requires callback and exception delegates plus valid Lua cancellation context.
Requires a live context, a valid managed SendOrPostCallback and state object, and has no per-item removal API.
Requires discovery and ownership of a live Browser MonoBehaviour and appends to that component's Action list; the component can be disabled or destroyed and supplies no external IPC.
The reviewed public surface queues domain-event closures rather than an arbitrary Action, depends on a live singleton/update consumer, and does not remove the managed callback or ingress requirement.
Requires a live MonoBehaviour, a typed callback, registration ownership, and guaranteed DelUpdate cleanup on every terminal path.
Requires a class-valid IPlayerLoopItem implementation and vtable whose MoveNext lifetime and cleanup are owned by the adapter.

required_ingress: A documented, user-authorized, lifecycle-owned in-process adapter entry must exist; remote thread creation, DLL injection, code patching, and fabricated delegate fields do not satisfy this contract.
The adapter must expose bounded authenticated local IPC and accept only a reviewed preset request, never raw RVAs, arbitrary method names, or executable payloads.
Any non-main adapter thread must attach to the current IL2CPP domain before using managed objects and must detach only after it releases its managed references.
required_callback: A precompiled IL2CPP-managed callback with a valid exact-build method descriptor must own the request state.
The callback target, Action, request, and receipt state must remain rooted until a terminal callback receipt; queue insertion alone is not a cancellation or shutdown lifetime protocol.
Cancellation is a callback-time fail-closed state transition because the selected queue has no removal API.
The callback must contain managed exceptions and must not permit native faults or exceptions to cross an unsupported ABI boundary.
queue_contract: Before queueing, verify the exact build, initialized PlayerLoopHelper class, nonzero mainThreadId, nonnull synchronization context, yielders index 8, class-valid Update queue, queue timing 8, and bounded consistent array counts.
Queue exactly one Action using UniTask.Post(action, Update=8, hidden MethodInfo null).
Use atomic queued, executing, canceled, succeeded, and failed request states; a canceled callback must execute as a no-op and publish a terminal receipt.
callback_contract: Reacquire current PlayerEnt, PlayerSkillInputComp, and ZSkillInputMgr inside the callback; do not use queue-time object pointers.

Recheck exact image identity, lifecycle generation, dungeon stage, scene/family/map, party leadership, marker slot-to-skill mapping, loading/transition/input blocking, idle marker lifecycle, and finite nonzero target inside the callback.
Call the reviewed SetIndicatorPos route, verify the staged indicator state and unchanged lifecycle, then call FirePlaySkillByIndicator for exactly one marker.
Publish the boolean dispatch result, but do not classify it as party-visible success without the matching passive inbound marker notification.
acknowledgement_contract: Permit only one marker in flight.
Require both game-owned dispatch success and a matching self inbound marker-add for the same scene, session, marker skill, and XYZ.
Abort on timeout, mismatch, leader loss, lifecycle change, scene change, replacement ambiguity, clear ambiguity, reconnect, or shutdown.
Do not advance markers 2 through 6 or reduce pacing until the preceding marker reaches the matched terminal state.

The lifecycle generation shared between queue-time validation and callback-time validation is not implemented.
Complete callback-time loading, scene-transition, cutscene, input-blocked, cooldown, replacement, and clear-state gates are not all resolved.
Atomicity between SetIndicatorPos and FirePlaySkillByIndicator against other indicator writers is not proven.

Server acceptance, rejection behavior, and safe pacing for a saved coordinate beyond the normal reticle range remain unproven.
